title: Visual Consistency and UI Quality knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Visual Consistency and UI Quality”?
options: Visual Consistency and UI Quality should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Visual Consistency and UI Quality helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Visual Consistency and UI Quality means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Visual Consistency and UI Quality removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Visual Consistency and UI Quality helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Visual Consistency and UI Quality is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Spacing and typography systems” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Spacing and typography systems” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Spacing and typography systems” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Spacing and typography systems” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Spacing and typography systems” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Spacing and typography systems” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Spacing and typography systems” under Visual Consistency and UI Quality. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Visual Consistency and UI Quality”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
